# REG-01: No Themes or Language Appealing to Minors

> Demo policy document for the NorthPlay legal approver agent (NorthPlay is a fictional operator). Fictional rules modelled on Ontario-style internet gaming advertising standards, written for hackathon use only; not legal advice and not any regulator's official text.

- **Rule ID:** REG-01
- **Category:** Protection of Minors
- **Source:** NorthPlay Advertising Policy (modelled on Ontario-style iGaming advertising standards), Section 2.03, Req. 1
- **Severity:** blocker
- **Jurisdiction:** Ontario, Canada

## Rule
Advertising must not be built on themes, or use language, intended to appeal primarily to minors.

## Intent
Keep gambling marketing from attracting people under the legal gambling age (19 in Ontario).

## What the reviewer checks for
- Youth slang, meme formats or school-related themes
- Video-game, toy, candy or back-to-school imagery
- Bright, childish visual style aimed at kids rather than adults
- References to youth sports leagues, high school or university varsity games

## Non-compliant examples
- "No cap, this parlay is bussin" with meme template visuals
- Ad framed around back-to-school season with lockers and backpacks

## Compliant examples
- Adult-oriented creative focused on the product, odds or the game itself, with standard disclaimers

## Remediation
Rewrite copy in neutral adult language and remove youth-oriented imagery or themes.

title: No Cartoons, Influencers or Celebrities Likely to Appeal to Minors
source: NorthPlay Advertising Policy (modelled on Ontario-style iGaming advertising standards), Section 2.03, Req. 3
rule: Advertising must not use cartoon figures, symbols, role models, social media influencers, celebrities or entertainers who would likely be expected to appeal to minors.
intent: Many personalities and animated characters have large under-19 audiences; using them reaches minors even if the ad is aimed at adults.
check_for: Animated mascots or cartoon characters
Social media creators, streamers or YouTubers with young audiences
Pop stars, actors or entertainers popular with teens
Emoji-heavy or sticker-style characters as the focal point
non_compliant: A cartoon hockey puck mascot cheering "Bet with Pucky!"
Popular teen gaming streamer promoting the app
compliant: Abstract brand graphics with no characters
An adult presenter with no youth-oriented following
remediation: Remove the character or personality. If a mascot is used, it must not primarily appeal to minors; when in doubt, remove it.

Advertising must not exploit the susceptibilities, aspirations, credulity, inexperience or lack of knowledge of potentially high-risk persons, or otherwise extoll the virtues of gaming. Protect people most vulnerable to gambling harm.

## Compliant examples
- Plain description of product features with responsible gambling message

## Remediation
Remove pressure, urgency and glorifying language; describe the product factually.

title: No Public Advertising of Bonuses, Credits or Inducements
source: NorthPlay Advertising Policy (modelled on Ontario-style iGaming advertising standards), Section 2.05

Advertising that communicates gambling inducements, bonuses and credits is prohibited, except on the operator's own gaming site and through direct marketing to players who have actively consented. This applies to all public advertising, including targeted and algorithm-based ads; inducements themselves are not banned.

## Intent
Bonus-driven public advertising was found to drive harmful sign-ups and play.

## What the reviewer checks for

title: 'Free' and 'Risk-Free' Claims and Terms Disclosure
source: NorthPlay Advertising Policy (modelled on Ontario-style iGaming advertising standards), Section 2.06
rule: Where inducement advertising is permitted (on-site or consented direct marketing), it must disclose all material conditions and limitations at first presentation (with other conditions no more than one click away); must not describe an offer as 'free' if the player must risk their own money or conditions attach to their money; and must not describe a bet as 'risk-free' if the player must incur any loss or risk their own money to use it or withdraw winnings.
intent: Players must understand the true cost and conditions of any offer.
check_for: The words 'free', 'free bet', 'risk-free', 'no risk', 'on us'
Offers requiring a deposit or wager to unlock
Missing wagering requirements, expiry, min odds or max payout
Terms hidden behind multiple clicks
non_compliant: Email: "Your risk-free first bet is waiting!" (requires $50 deposit)
On-site banner with bonus but no wagering terms shown
compliant: "Bet $50, get $50 in bonus bets. 1x playthrough, min odds -200, expires in 7 days. Full terms."
remediation: Remove 'free'/'risk-free' unless literally true; show material terms at first presentation.

- The words 'free', 'free bet', 'risk-free', 'no risk', 'on us'
- Offers requiring a deposit or wager to unlock
- Missing wagering requirements, expiry, min odds or max payout
- Terms hidden behind multiple clicks

## Non-compliant examples
- Email: "Your risk-free first bet is waiting!" (requires $50 deposit)
- On-site banner with bonus but no wagering terms shown

## Compliant examples
- "Bet $50, get $50 in bonus bets. 1x playthrough, min odds -200, expires in 7 days. Full terms."

## Remediation
Remove 'free'/'risk-free' unless literally true; show material terms at first presentation.

# REG-15: Direct Marketing Consent and Self-Excluded Player Suppression

> Demo policy document for the NorthPlay legal approver agent (NorthPlay is a fictional operator). Fictional rules modelled on Ontario-style internet gaming advertising standards, written for hackathon use only; not legal advice and not any regulator's official text.

- **Rule ID:** REG-15
- **Category:** Targeting & Consent
- **Source:** NorthPlay Advertising Policy (modelled on Ontario-style iGaming advertising standards), Section 2.07 and Standard 2.03 (no targeting of self-excluded or high-risk persons)
- **Severity:** blocker
- **Jurisdiction:** Ontario, Canada

## Rule
Players must actively opt in before receiving direct marketing of inducements, bonuses and credits, and must be able to withdraw consent at any time. Marketing must not target self-excluded, centrally self-excluded, underage or known high-risk persons.

## Intent
Direct marketing is the only permitted bonus channel, so consent and suppression must be airtight.

## What the reviewer checks for
- Email/SMS/push creative without an unsubscribe or opt-out mechanism
- Audience definitions that include lapsed, self-excluded or high-risk segments
- 'Win-back' campaigns aimed at players who stopped playing
- Lookalike audiences seeded from high-loss players

## Non-compliant examples
- SMS with bonus offer and no opt-out instructions
- "We miss you!" bonus campaign to players inactive after self-exclusion

## Compliant examples
- Consented email with clear unsubscribe link, audience scrubbed against self-exclusion lists

## Remediation
Add opt-out, confirm consent flags, and scrub audience against self-exclusion and high-risk lists.
